comparison_intro: Flag the beginning and end of each sorted group, keeping every row. Endpoints are explicit, including a data set with one row.

language_notes.sas: Macro transform supplies source/result names. BY group creates FIRST.group and LAST.group, including both endpoints of a singleton.
language_notes.python: translate checks sorted, nonmissing group values before these comparisons. Explicit iloc endpoints also work with nullable strings.
language_notes.r: out <- df precedes this excerpt. translate validates sorted, nonmissing groups. Integer vectors and explicit endpoints handle a singleton.

semantic_notes.title: Output and instructions both matter
semantic_notes.text: Historical B2/B3 summaries match the fixture but omit explicit endpoint handling. This reference honors that requirement; trial scores stay unchanged.

semantic_notes.title: Keep the whole row sequence
semantic_notes.text: These flags annotate every record. Filtering to only boundary rows drops id 4 in the original fixture and changes the operation.

tests.name: Original known-answer fixture
tests.input: Groups A,A,B,B,B,C in original id order 1-6.
tests.catches: Wrong boundary direction, lost interior rows or mishandled one-row group C.

tests.name: Added one-row data set
tests.input: One row: id=41, group=Z, value=99; Python uses nullable strings.
tests.expected: Both integer flags equal 1; exactly one row remains.
tests.catches: Reliance on NA comparisons, endpoint omissions, and two-row minimum assumptions.

tests.name: Preserve rows and integer flags
tests.input: Original fixture with non-default Python/R row labels.
tests.expected: Input and source order unchanged; complete correct integer 0/1 flags.
tests.catches: Index-label endpoints, row filtering/reordering, input mutation or string/boolean flag outputs.

scope: One sorted, nonmissing group key. The one-row edge case is added local validation. No claim covers multiple BY variables, missing groups or NOTSORTED input.
